## Two journeys {#ss5-two-journeys .gp-lesson .gp-journeys}

Your starting size is $L$. Your friend's starting size is $U$.

<p class="gp-journeys-task">Complete the next three rows.</p>

```{=html}
<table class="gp-journeys-table" aria-label="Sizes at one-second intervals">
  <thead><tr><th scope="col">Time elapsed</th><th scope="col">Your size</th><th scope="col">Your friend's size</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><th scope="row">0 seconds</th><td><span data-math="L">L</span></td><td><span data-math="U">U</span></td></tr>
    <tr><th scope="row">1 second</th><td><span class="fragment" data-fragment-index="0"><span data-math="10L">10L</span></span></td><td><span class="fragment" data-fragment-index="0"><span data-math="0.1U">0.1U</span></span></td></tr>
    <tr><th scope="row">2 seconds</th><td><span class="fragment" data-fragment-index="0"><span data-math="100L">100L</span></span></td><td><span class="fragment" data-fragment-index="0"><span data-math="0.01U">0.01U</span></span></td></tr>
    <tr><th scope="row">3 seconds</th><td><span class="fragment" data-fragment-index="0"><span data-math="1000L">1000L</span></span></td><td><span class="fragment" data-fragment-index="0"><span data-math="0.001U">0.001U</span></span></td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```

<p class="gp-journeys-question">Consider each sequence: <strong>What is staying constant in this sequence?</strong></p>

::: {.gp-journeys-multipliers .fragment data-fragment-index="1"}
Your sequence: multiply by **$10$**.  
Your friend's sequence: divide by $10$, or multiply by **$0.1$**.
:::

::: {.takeaway .fragment data-fragment-index="2"}
Both are **geometric sequences**: multiply each term by a fixed number to get the next term.
:::

::: notes

Initially only the starting values L and U are visible. Both are positive lengths measured in the same unit, with L much smaller than U. Ask students to supply the next three rows. First click reveals all six missing entries. Ask the open question for each column: “What is staying constant in this sequence?” Give students time to articulate the repeated multiplication themselves.

Second click reveals the multipliers 10 and 0.1. Dividing by 10 is equivalent to multiplying by 0.1. Third click reveals that both sequences are geometric. A geometric sequence can decrease as well as increase. The following slide develops the definition with examples and non-examples.

Time 0 gives the first listed term. Later, when using a_n=ar^(n−1), term n corresponds to n−1 elapsed seconds. Connect this table to the preceding estimate: L≈10^−35 m and U≈10^27 m. After 31 seconds, both rounded models give 10^−4 m, or 0.1 mm, consistent with the video's approximate human-egg-cell comparison. The growing sequence reaches U after 62 seconds. The 31-second equality is exact for the rounded powers-of-ten model. More precise starting lengths need not produce equality at a whole-second sample.

Context: the Short and the teacher-supplied continuation summary on the preceding slides. The full-video link is for optional viewing later. The table is the mathematical model obtained by applying the stated scale factors.

:::
